questions.question_text:
Students want a record of travel modes used as children enter the playground this morning.
Which collection method best matches the task?

options.text: Watch at the entrance and tally each child once.
Ask children next month to remember this morning.
options.why: This delays collection and relies on memory instead of recording visible arrivals.

options.text: Guess the travel modes from the bicycles left nearby.
options.why: This misses other modes and does not observe every child entering.

options.text: Count every child without recording a travel mode.
options.why: This gives only a total and loses the categories the task requires.

questions.solution_text: Direct observation records the visible mode immediately, with each child tallied once.

questions.question_text:
The bicycle tally is $||||$.
Another cyclist enters.
Which tally should now be recorded?

options.why: This leaves the tally unchanged and fails to record the new cyclist.
This records two new marks, increasing four to six instead of five.
This removes an existing mark instead of adding the new observation.

questions.solution_text: The fifth result crosses the group of four, giving $\cancel{||||}$.

questions.question_text: What frequency is shown by the scooter tally $\cancel{||||}\;\cancel{||||}\;||||$?

options.why: This counts only the two complete groups of five and ignores four marks.
This counts one group of five and the final four, omitting another full group.
This treats the final group of four as if it were a complete group of five.

questions.question_text:
A child walks into the playground while carrying, but not riding, a skateboard.
The categories are walk, bicycle, scooter, skateboard and other.
What should the observer record?

options.why: This classifies the object being carried as the travel mode actually used.

options.text: One mark for walk and one for skateboard
options.why: This records one child twice even though only one travel mode was used.
Walking already has a matching named category, so other is unnecessary.

questions.solution_text: The observed travel mode is walking, so record exactly one walk mark.

questions.question_text:
Arrivals are observed in this order: scooter, bicycle, walk, walk, scooter, walk, bicycle.
Which set of frequencies is correct?

options.why: Records the third arrival as a scooter, moving one walk into the scooter column.
Stops recording after the sixth arrival, so the final bicycle is never tallied.
Makes both slips at once: one walk logged as a scooter and the last bicycle missed.

questions.solution_text: Walk appears $3$ times, scooter $2$ times and bicycle $2$ times; $3+2+2=7$.

questions.question_text:
Exactly $24$ children enter the playground.
The recorded travel-mode frequencies are walk $11$, scooter $6$, bicycle $5$ and other $3$.
What does the check show?

options.text: One result was recorded twice or one extra mark was added.

options.why: A missing result would make the tally total smaller than 24, not larger.

options.text: The records match the observed total exactly.
options.why: The frequencies add to 25, which is one more than the 24 children observed.
Two duplicated results would give a total of 26 rather than the recorded 25.

questions.solution_text:
$11+6+5+3=25$
The tally total is one too high, so one extra record was made.
